concerns.text: T002's verification says the raw JSONLs 'pass schema validation', but dataset.schema.yaml lists cyclomatic_complexity, nesting_depth, per_token_loss, and token_count as required fields — none exist at download time. The task's own verification is unexecutable as written; either name a reduced raw-stage schema or move schema validation to the annotated/inference stage.

T004 says outputs are written 'per code_chunk.schema.yaml' but then lists flat fields (per_token_loss, entropy, ngram_probability, token_count, status). code_chunk.schema.yaml mandates a nested structure (static_labels/inference_metrics/metadata, additionalProperties: false, required baseline_model). An implementer cannot satisfy both instructions; pick one target schema and state it.

T004 bundles two substantial deliverables (KenLM baseline training/scoring AND the full CPU inference engine with retry logic) plus two test files into one task. Too coarse for deterministic execution; split so each artifact (ngram.py, engine.py) is its own task with its own verification.

T005 says correlation_stats.json carries 'p_value placeholder from permutation later', but correlation_result.schema.yaml requires p_value as a number with no placeholder convention defined. State what value is written pre-T009 (e.g., NaN is invalid per schema; use 1.0 or defer writing the file until T009) so the intermediate artifact is schema-valid and the T005 verification is checkable.

T001 bundles environment repair, config, quickstart, and multiple rejected-artifact repairs into one task with a multi-part verification. Consider splitting the pinned-requirements/environment fix from the config/quickstart setup so each verification (pip install succeeds; quickstart command exists) attaches to a single deliverable.
